description_full: Ithaca Energy plc, together with its subsidiaries, engages in the development and production of oil and gas in the North Sea. It owns a portfolio of assets located in the Northern, Central, and Southern North Sea, as well as West of Shetland and the Moray Firth areas of the UK Continental Shelf. The company was formerly known as Delek North Sea Limited and changed its name to Ithaca Energy plc in October 2022. The company was incorporated in 2004 and is based in London, the United Kingdom. Ithaca Energy plc operates as a subsidiary of DKL Energy Limited.

financial_summary: Ithaca Energy plc is a mid-cap energy business with a $6.5B market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are contracting by -2.6pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 15% against a 9% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 43%.
The business throws off $861M in free cash flow — roughly 29 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -21.7% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 8.3×.

Management returns a meaningful 7.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 87% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
